title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SUPPORT TO SPACE STARTUPS
body_text:
As per the DPIIT Start-up India Portal , around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to carry out various space activities, out of which 18 are start-ups. The details are as under:
Agnikul Cosmos Pvt Ltd, Akshath Aerospace Private Limited, Azista BST, Bellatrix Aerospace Pvt Ltd, Cosmoserv Space India Private Limited, Dhruva Space Private Limited, Digantara Research and Technologies Pvt. Ltd GalaxEye Space Solutions Private Limited, HEX20Labs India Pvt ltd., Inorbit Space Telecommunications Private Limited, Manastu Space Technologies Private Limited, NSpace Tech India Private Limited, OrbitAID Aerospace Private Limited, PierSight Space Private Limited, PixxelSpace India Private Limited, Skyroot Aerospace Private Limited, Space Kidz India, TakeMe2Space Technologies Pvt. Ltd,
Further, the details of facilitation provided to start-ups by IN SPACe including launch slots and testing access, year-wise are as under:
Sl. No. Year Details of Start-ups Facilitation provided 1 2022 Agnikul Cosmos, Skyroot Aerospace, Pixxel Flex seal & acoustic testing, S/X-band antenna RF testing, sub-orbital launch access (Vikram-S), launch vehicle TM reception. 2 2023 Dhruva Space, Pixxel Space, Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos, Spacekidz, Azista BST Agniban SoRTeD launch access, RAMAN-I & II engine testing, Azaadisat-2 environmental testing, static stage testing, ground station support. 3 2024 Skyroot Aerospace, Pixxel Space, Manastu Space, Piersight Space, N Space Tech India Pvt. Ltd. Stage-1 casting & propellant supply, hardware-in-loop simulations, POEM payload EMI/EMC and shock testing. 4 2025 Agnikul Cosmos, Dhruva Space, Piersight, Galaxeye, Satleo Labs, Skyroot Aerospace Cryogenic pump PDR review, X/UHF-band downlink support, TVAC/outgassing tests, trajectory validation, cooling umbilical supply. 5 2026 TakeMe2Space, Bellatrix Aerospace, Skyroot Aerospace, OrbitAid Aerospace, Dhruva Space Pvt. Ltd, First Launch Pad (FLP) utilization for Vikram-1, docking mechanism lab testing, SRS shock testing, silicide coating for micro-thrusters.
The State-wise details of number of recognised space start-ups are not available with                     IN-SPACe.
Details of funds sanctioned and disbursed by IN-SPACe as on 31.07.2026 during the last five years are as under:
(Rs in Lakhs)
Sl. No. Name of Scheme Project/ Scheme Envelope Cumulative FY 2022-23 FY 2023-24 FY 2024-25 FY 2025-26 FY 2026-27 1 IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme/PIE 6500 NIL 56 88.3 225 20 389.30 2 Venture Capital Funds 100000 SEBI Approval: 31-10-2025 605.64 18287.40 18893.04 3 Technology adoption Fund 50000 03 NGE selected for development of Technology NIL NIL NIL 4 Satellite Bus as a Service (SBaas) 7500 03 NGE selected for development NIL 750 750 5 Common Technical facilities 50000 Agreement signed with Govt. of Gujarat and Tamilnadu NIL NIL NIL Total 214000 0 88.3 56 830.64 13077.15 20032.34
IN-SPACe has established a digital platform to facilitate startups in accessing various schemes and services.  The platform serves as a single-window interface for enabling and supporting the growth of India's space startups. Through this platform, startups can apply for Authorisation, funding opportunities, seek mentorship, access ISRO/IN-SPACe facilities, avail technology transfer, receive launch and mission support, and participate in skill development and capacity-building programmes.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and
Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed government support to India's space startups: about 440 space-tech startups are registered on the DPIIT Start-up India Portal, and IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, of which 18 are startups. The reply listed year-wise facilitation (launch slots, testing access) provided since 2022 to startups like Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Dhruva Space and others, and disclosed IN-SPACe's fund disbursements (Seed Fund, Venture Capital Funds, Technology Adoption Fund, SBaaS, Common Technical Facilities) totalling about Rs 200 crore over five years as of 31 July 2026.
enrichment.context:
IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) was set up in 2020 as a single-window, independent nodal agency under the Department of Space to authorise, promote and regulate private/non-government participation in space activities, following the 2020 space sector reforms that ended ISRO's monopoly. This reply reflects the government's push to build a commercial space ecosystem, supplementing the 2023 Indian Space Policy, the 2024 relaxation of FDI norms in space (up to 100% in some segments), and the establishment of NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) as ISRO's commercial arm. Financial instruments such as the IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme, a proposed Rs 1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for space startups (with SEBI approval), and infrastructure-sharing schemes like Satellite Bus as a Service and Common Technical Facilities are meant to reduce entry barriers for startups needing capital-intensive testing and launch access, which were historically monopolised by ISRO.

The reply is significant for tracking India's ambition to capture a larger share of the global space economy, targeting an eight-fold growth of India's space economy by 2033 as stated in national space policy documents. It also highlights persistent gaps, such as the absence of state-wise data on recognised space startups, and slow fund utilisation in schemes like the Technology Adoption Fund and Common Technical Facilities, indicating implementation challenges even as headline startup and authorisation numbers grow.

prelims_questions.question: IN-SPACe, which authorises and promotes private participation in India's space sector, functions under which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) is an autonomous nodal agency established under the Department of Space to authorise and promote non-government space activities.

prelims_questions.question: Consider the following schemes/funds mentioned in relation to India's space startup ecosystem: 1. IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme 2. Satellite Bus as a Service (SBaaS) 3. Technology Adoption Fund. Which of the above are administered/facilitated by IN-SPACe to support space startups?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release lists all three—Seed Fund Scheme, SBaaS, and Technology Adoption Fund—as schemes under IN-SPACe's funding envelope to support startups and non-government entities.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of India's 2020 space sector reforms in fostering a private space startup ecosystem. Evaluate the role of IN-SPACe in providing regulatory, technical, and financial support to such startups.

India's space economy is projected to grow multi-fold in the coming decade, driven partly by private startups. What structural and financial challenges hinder the scaling up of space startups in India, and what policy measures can address them?
